DATA LINEAGE

From public records to an auditable view.

Your linked Kaggle Chicago Crime dataset is a BigQuery-backed listing, not a downloadable CSV. Its metadata identifies the City of Chicago as the source.

This dashboard independently retrieves aggregates from the City of Chicago Crimes — 2001 to Present dataset (ijzp-q8t2). It is a new implementation, not a recovery of your original app or a copy of the Kaggle snapshot.

Window
January 1, 2024–December 31, 2025, by incident date

Published incident records; homicides may be recorded per victim

Temporal aggregate
Year × month × offense × weekday × hour
Boundary source
City of Chicago community boundaries

STATISTICAL METHODS

What these measures mean.

Counts versus rates

Incident counts are not population-adjusted crime rates. The optional citywide per-100,000 view uses a fixed 2020 Census Chicago population of 2,746,388 (U.S. Census QuickFacts). It is an illustrative denominator, not a contemporaneous estimate. It is unavailable for individual communities.

Arrest proportion & uncertainty

Arrest = true records divided by selected records. The interval uses the Wilson score method (z = 1.96). It describes a binomial model, not uncertainty from underreporting or classification errors. An arrest is not a conviction, and this proportion is not a case-clearance rate.

Temporal comparison

2025 and 2024 are calendar-aligned. Percentage change is (2025 − 2024) / 2024. Earlier-year selection has no prior-year comparison because 2023 is outside this snapshot. Revisions and classification changes limit interpretation; the publisher cautions against comparisons over time.

Exploratory model

Ordinary least squares estimates a straight trend over the selected monthly series. The displayed three-month intervals use t critical values and residual variance, clipped at zero. Autocorrelation, seasonality, outliers and reporting delays can invalidate these assumptions. No causal inference, predictive policing, or validated prediction is claimed.

LIMITATIONS & RESPONSIBLE USE

The missing context matters.

Reports may be unverified, reclassified, delayed, incomplete or duplicated. Counts are influenced by population, visitors, land use, reporting behavior and enforcement. Lower recorded crime does not necessarily imply lower victimization.

Community comparisons use counts only. No neighborhood risk scores or individual-level predictions are produced. The map shows administrative community areas, not precise incident locations.

Zero monthly cells mean zero records in the retrieved aggregate, not proof that no crime occurred. Unknown community codes remain included in city totals. The dashboard does not contain names, street addresses, case IDs or personal data.

MACHINE LEARNING / TEMPORAL VALIDATION

Show the evaluation, not just a prediction.

One-day-ahead citywide incident counts. Three models. Four forward evaluation windows.

Fixed experiment: all offenses, citywide, full daily series. Dashboard filters do not apply. This is retrospective evaluation, using observed prior-day incident counts; reporting delays are not modeled.
OUT-OF-TIME BENCHMARK

Earn the improvement

2024 initial training; quarterly refits through 2025. Lower error is better.

MODEL CARD

What the model knows

Leakage controls

  • Lag and rolling features are shifted before the target day.
  • Scaling is fitted on training folds only.
  • Chronological quarterly splits; no random shuffling.
  • Hyperparameters are fixed, with deterministic seeds.
  • No arrest outcomes, locations of people, or future incident counts are used as target-day predictors.

These experiments predict aggregate counts, not individual behavior or community safety.

ACTUAL VERSUS PREDICTED

Inspect the mistakes

Zoom the chart or select a quarter to inspect daily errors.

DESCRIPTIVE ANOMALY SCREEN

Find days worth investigating

Deviation from the preceding 28-day mean, scaled by preceding sample standard deviation.

This is a statistical screening rule, not an ML classifier or significance test. Seasonality, multiple comparisons, revisions and reporting artifacts can trigger flags; no cause is inferred.

REPRODUCIBLE BUILD

Python. SQL. Plotly Dash.

The public site is a static JavaScript application with Plotly.js and in-browser SQLite. The downloadable source also includes a runnable Python Plotly Dash application with linked maps, trends, filters, and CSV export. 

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python pipeline/prepare.py
python pipeline/models.py
python dash_app/app.py

To refresh source records, run python pipeline/extract.py. Network access to the public Chicago API is required. Re-running extraction may produce revised totals.
